issues.display_title: Issue #4084: Fix Issue Sub Location Not Working Correctly
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Bug Report: Sub Locations not working correctly (reported by a photographer, account user_id: 253).

The Sub Location management on the Photographer Location / Set Location page behaves inconsistently — duplicate entries appear, a false "maximum" error is triggered, and saved sub-locations don't match what the user entered after reload.

Initial Situation

User status is "pending". They want to set up the following locations:

  • Headquarters: Basel, Switzerland
  • Branch offices: Lucerne, Zurich, Bern

Steps / Observed Behavior (the bug)

  1. Lucerne appeared twice in the sub-location list. The user deleted the duplicate entry.
  2. Clicking "Next" triggered the error message: "Maximum 4 sublocations allowed per photographer" — even though only 3 branch offices were intended.
  3. After reloading the page, a new inconsistency appeared: Bern is now listed twice, and Lucerne is missing from the map.

The behaviour is inconsistent and cannot be reproduced in a controlled manner.

Expected Result

  • Headquarters: Basel, Switzerland
  • Branch offices: Lucerne, Zurich, Bern

(i.e. exactly the sub-locations the user entered — no duplicates, no missing entries, no false "maximum" error.)

Acceptance Criteria

  1. Sub-locations save exactly as entered — no duplicate entries are created or persisted.
  2. The "Maximum 4 sublocations allowed per photographer" validation only triggers when more than 4 sub-locations actually exist (deleted duplicates are not counted).
  3. After saving and reloading, the sub-location list and the map markers accurately reflect the user's intended entries (Basel HQ + Lucerne, Zurich, Bern) with no missing or duplicated pins.
  4. The behavior is consistent and reproducible (no state desync between the list, the saved data, and the map).

Reference: docs/superpowers/specs/analyze-all.md — see §4 (Photographer profile & directory) and §12 (Maps). Affected user user_id: 253.

issues.display_title: Issue #4088: Align Dropbox upload flow with Google Drive (Dropbox Chooser)
issues.main_description_html:
Context

Dropbox upload currently differs a lot from Google Drive. Google Drive uses the native Google Picker: click button → pick files → auto-upload. Dropbox uses a custom-built folder browser that requires connecting a Dropbox account (OAuth), forces files into a specific "GoThru" folder, and only lets users select whole folders (not individual files).

This is inconsistent UX and extra maintenance.

Goal

Make Dropbox behave like Google Drive by adopting Dropbox Chooser (Dropbox's native file picker, the equivalent of Google Picker).

Scope

  • Replace the existing custom Dropbox flow entirely (folder browser, OAuth account connect, "GoThru" folder requirement).
  • The existing Dropbox tab: single button → opens native Dropbox Chooser → user picks individual files (multi-select) → auto-upload, same as Google Drive.
  • Files upload to the currently selected level, matching Google Drive behavior.

Payload

Dropbox Chooser does not return an access token. Per picked file it returns a temporary direct download link (requested via linkType: "direct", expires ~4h). Uploads use a new source: "dropbox-chooser" (separate backend branch — tracked separately).

FE → POST /panoramas/upload (FormData, one request per file):

field value
token_pano upload ticket from GET /panoramas/token?mid=&level=
source "dropbox-chooser"
file the Chooser link (direct download URL)

Example:

token_pano:  <token>
source:      dropbox-chooser
file:        https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/.../pano_01.jpg

Acceptance criteria

  • The Dropbox tab shows a single "Open Dropbox" button (no account-connect step).
  • Clicking it opens the native Dropbox Chooser.
  • User can multi-select individual .jpg/.jpeg files.
  • Selected files auto-upload to the active level.
  • Upload progress + result popup behave like Google Drive.
  • Old Dropbox flow (folder browser, OAuth connect, GoThru folder) removed.

Out of scope

  • Changes to Google Drive or local Browse upload.
  • Backend source: "dropbox-chooser" handling (separate project).

issues.display_title: Issue #4108: Fix AI Blur Modal: Rename to "Free AI Tokens", Conditional Display & Correct "Free Tokens Applied" Label
issues.main_description_html:
Description

Follow-up corrections to the AI Blur order-summary modal (the free/paid AI token breakdown from #4083), based on feedback on the live UI.

In the current modal (example: Order Summary for 48 Images, 19 free AI tokens available), two labeling/visibility issues were flagged:

  1. Wrong label — "Remaining AI Tokens" should be "Free AI Tokens". The balance row at the top of the summary currently reads "Remaining AI Tokens"; it should read "Free AI Tokens" since it represents the free token bucket.
  2. Conditional display. This Free AI Tokens row (and its applied sub-row) should only be displayed when the user actually has free tokens. If there are no free tokens, do not render the row at all.
  3. Wrong sub-row label — "Paid Credits Applied" should be "Free Tokens Applied". In the screenshot, the deduction sub-row shows "Paid Credits Applied -19 AI Tokens", but those 19 deducted tokens are the free tokens being consumed — so this sub-row must be labeled "Free Tokens Applied" (green), not "Paid Credits Applied".

Scope

  • Rename the "Remaining AI Tokens" label to "Free AI Tokens" in the AI Blur order summary.
  • Render the Free AI Tokens balance row only when free tokens > 0; hide it entirely when there are none.
  • Ensure the deduction of free tokens is labeled "Free Tokens Applied" (not "Paid Credits Applied"), and only shown when free tokens are actually applied.
  • Keep "Paid Credits Applied" labeling reserved for actual paid/subscription credit deductions.

Acceptance Criteria

  1. The top balance row reads "Free AI Tokens" (not "Remaining AI Tokens").
  2. When the user has 0 free tokens, the Free AI Tokens row and its applied sub-row are not displayed at all.
  3. When free tokens are consumed, the sub-row is labeled "Free Tokens Applied" (green) with the correct negative amount.
  4. The "Paid Credits Applied" label only appears for genuine paid/subscription credit deductions.
  5. Totals (Total Cost, Tokens required, Saved for Later) remain correct and unchanged.

Reference: docs/brains/2026-06-17-ai-blur-free-token-balance-design.md and docs/superpowers/specs/analyze-all.md §5.2 (Token micropayments). Refines #4083; file: src/pages/Tour/Detail/Blur/Components/AIBlurModal.jsx.

Note from Developer

This has already been implemented under the following conditions:

  • If a user has free tokens available, the system displays "Free AI Tokens" and "Free Tokens Applied".
  • If the free tokens are used up, these labels are not shown.
  • 1 tokens = 20 AI tokens. If a user only uses part of their tokens, the remainder stays available for later use.
  • Because of this, "Remaining AI Tokens" and "Paid Credits Applied" are shown to indicate that there are still leftover AI tokens from a previous purchase.

issues.display_title: Issue #4121: Consolidate "Check Archive" Logic into the Main "Unarchive" Button
issues.main_description_html:
Description

The current workflow for unarchiving a tour is causing user friction. Users are unaware that they need to click the small "Check Archive" icon button before clicking the main green "Unarchive from Google" button.

To streamline this process and improve the user experience, we need to consolidate these two actions. The small "Check Archive" button should be removed entirely. Instead, the main "Unarchive from Google" button should open the Unarchive Modal, and clicking the confirm button inside the modal should automatically perform the archive check first. If the check confirms there is data to unarchive, it should seamlessly proceed with the unarchiving process.

Sub task

  • My Tour
  • Tour Detail

Acceptance Criteria

  1. The standalone "Check Archive" button is no longer visible on the Tour Details screen.
  2. Clicking "Unarchive from Google" opens the Unarchive Modal.
  3. Clicking the "Unarchive" (Confirm) button inside the modal successfully triggers the archive check in the background.
  4. If archived data exists, the system automatically proceeds to unarchive it without requiring additional clicks, and shows a 5-second countdown on the confirm button upon success before closing the modal without reloading.
  5. The user receives clear visual feedback (loading indicators, success/error messages) throughout the newly consolidated process.

Test Scenario (for Tester / QA)

Preconditions

  • Access to a Google Business / Street View tour that is currently archived on Google (has data to unarchive)
  • Also have a tour that is not archived (nothing to unarchive) for the negative case.
  • Open the Tour Details screen.

Scenario 1 — "Check Archive" button removed

  1. Open Tour Details for any tour.
  2. ✅ Expected: The standalone small "Check Archive" icon button is no longer present anywhere on the screen. Only the main "Unarchive from Google" button remains.

Scenario 2 — Unarchive via Modal (happy path)

  1. On an archived tour, click "Unarchive from Google" to open the modal.
  2. Click the "Unarchive" button inside the modal.
  3. ✅ Expected: The system automatically runs the archive check in the background, finds archived data, and proceeds to unarchive — all without any extra clicks.
  4. ✅ Expected: On success, the tour's images/data are restored, a success message is shown, and the modal's confirm button displays a 5-second countdown before closing without a page reload.

Scenario 3 — Nothing to unarchive

  1. On a tour with no archived data, click "Unarchive from Google" to open the modal.
  2. Click the "Unarchive" button inside the modal.
  3. ✅ Expected: The check runs, finds nothing to unarchive, and the user gets a clear message (e.g. "No archived data to restore") — no silent failure, no stuck spinner.

Scenario 4 — Visual feedback during the process

  1. Click the confirm button in the modal on an archived tour and observe the button/UI while it works.
  2. ✅ Expected: A loading indicator is shown during the check + unarchive; the button is disabled/spinner-state to prevent double-clicks; a clear success or error message appears at the end.

Scenario 5 — Error handling

  1. Simulate/encounter a failure during the check or unarchive (e.g. network/API error).
  2. ✅ Expected: A clear error message is shown, and the button returns to its normal clickable state so the user can retry (no infinite spinner).

Pass criteria: The "Check Archive" button is gone, the "Unarchive from Google" modal acts as the single point of entry, checking and unarchiving seamlessly happen upon confirmation, and the user always sees clear loading/success/error feedback.

Reference: docs/superpowers/specs/analyze-all.md — see §4 (Publishing: archive/unarchive handling).
